title: bide flow config
description: A bide plan flow declared as data (YAML or JSON), read by plan.Load, bide check and bide view -config. Every key is snake_case. Block, predicate and merge names refer to Go code registered in a plan.Registry.

version.description: Config format version. Required; this release reads only 1.

flow.description: The flow's label, used in diagrams, conformance and the topology digest.

in.description: Optional input type name, documentation only. Load cross-checks it against the Go In type.

out.description: Optional output type name, documentation only. Load cross-checks it against the Go Out type.

entry.description: Name of the entry node. When omitted, the first node in nodes is the entry.

nodes.description: The steps, in order. The order is part of the topology digest.

wiring.description: Ordered edges, switches and joins. Each element sets exactly one of edge, switch or join.

assert.description: Policy assertions about the graph, one per line. Checked by bide check and bide view -config; plan.Load ignores them and they are not part of the digest.
examples: every path to charge passes approval >= 2 of 3
every path to a terminal passes validate

safety.description: Retry-on-resume class. readonly and idempotent re-run after a crash; side_effect halts and asks for the outcome. A config may keep or lower the level the Go registration declares, never raise it.

approval.description: An m-of-n human approval gate: the run pauses before the node until need of the approvers have signed.

need.description: How many approvals are required, between 1 and the number of approvers.

approvers.description: The bounded set of approver ids (printable ASCII, distinct ignoring case).

exclude_principal.description: Separation of duties: never count a decision by the run's requester (the principal the run was started for, its identity's on_behalf_of). A run with no requester is refused at the gate, and so is one whose requester is an approver when need is then out of reach.

node.description: One step: its journal name and the registered block it runs.

name.description: The node's name in the journal and in wiring.

block.description: The name of the block registered in the plan.Registry.

safety.description: Lower the retry class of this node. Omitted keeps what the block's Go registration declares.

approval.description: Gate this node behind an m-of-n approval. Omitted keeps the gate the block declares, if any.

arm.description: One arm of a switch: the predicate and the node it routes to.

pred.description: The registered predicate name. Its input type must equal the switched node's output type.

to.description: The node this arm routes to.

loop_max.description: When above 0, makes this arm a bounded loop-back to an earlier node (an ancestor of the switch): it runs again while pred holds, up to loop_max iterations. 0 or omitted is an ordinary forward arm.

wire.description: One wiring element: an edge, a switch or a join.

edge.description: [from, to]: the output of from feeds to.

switch.description: The node whose output is switched over. It routes only through its arms.

else.description: The fallback node when no arm matches. Omitted means no else arm.

join.description: The fan-in node's name. It must not be a declared node; the join creates it.

inputs.description: The upstream nodes, one per merge-block parameter, in order.

merge.description: The merge block registered with RegisterJoin2 or RegisterJoin3.

safety.description: Lower the join node's retry class. Without it, the merge block's registered options apply (none: a side effect).

approval.description: Gate the join node behind an m-of-n approval.

assertion.description: A policy assertion. A node is named bare (no spaces) or in double quotes.

anyOf.title: approval gate on every path
anyOf.description: every path to <node> passes approval >= K [of N] [excluding the requester]

anyOf.title: every path to a terminal passes a node
anyOf.description: every path to a terminal passes <node>

anyOf.title: every path to a node passes a node
no side effect after a node

examples: every path to charge passes approval >= 2 of 3
every path to charge passes approval >= 1
every path to charge passes approval >= 2 of 3 excluding the requester
every path to charge passes validate
every path to a terminal passes validate
